title: Youth At Every Decision-Making Table Grant 2026: $2,000 Grants for U.S. Organizations to Build Youth Leadership and Decision-Making Opportunities
summary: The Youth At Every Decision-Making Table Grant 2026 is a new funding opportunity from Youth Service America (YSA) , supported by an AmeriCorps MLK Day of Service grant , designed to help organizations create or strengthen formal structures through which young people can participate in leadership, decision-making, community service, and civic engagement. The grant will provide $2,000 to selected organizations that want to develop a new Youth Council or a similar youth leadership structure, or expand an existing one. In addition to establishing or strengthening youth leadership structures, grantees will be expected to organize a citywide, regional, or statewide Youth Leadership Summit around Martin Luther King Jr. Day and create continuing opportunities for youth voice, leadership, and decision-making through The Civic Season, from Juneteenth through July 4 . The program is particularly focused on ensuring that young people are not simply consulted occasionally but have meaningful opportunities to participate in organizational and community decision-making. YSA states that the grant program is intended to support the development or expansion of youth councils and similar structures while engaging at least 200 youth and adults in training or youth voice, leadership, and decision-making opportunities. Youth At Every Decision-Making Table Grant 2026: Overview Youth Service America is accepting applications from eligible U.S.-based organizations seeking funding to strengthen youth participation and leadership. The opportunity is connected to the MLK Day of Service , which will take place on January 18, 2027 . YSA s MLK Day of Service campaign describes the holiday as a national day of service focused on community action, service, and honoring the legacy of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. For this particular grant, organizations will use the funding to create or expand structures that give young people a more formal role in organizational and community decision-making. Key details at a glance Opportunity: Youth At Every Decision-Making Table Grant Organizer: Youth Service America (YSA) Funding: AmeriCorps MLK Day of Service grant Grant amount: $2,000 per selected grantee Total funding available: $50,000 Number of organizations expected to receive grants: 25 Required local match: $1,000 in cash or in-kind support Minimum engagement requirement: 200 youth and adults Main focus: Youth voice, leadership, decision-making, youth councils, youth leadership structures, and community service MLK Day of Service: January 18, 2027 Application deadline: Sunday, October 25, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. local time Geographic eligibility: United States organizations meeting the program s organizational eligibility requirements Application format: Online application Contact: Mike Minks at mminks@ysa.org YSA s official MLK Day of Service page confirms that the program will award $2,000 grants, with $50,000 available overall and 25 citywide, regional, or statewide organizations expected to receive funding. What Is the Youth At Every Decision-Making Table Grant? The Youth At Every Decision-Making Table Grant is designed around the idea that young people should have meaningful opportunities to contribute to decisions affecting their organizations and communities. Rather than supporting only a one-time service event, the grant focuses on developing or expanding ongoing youth leadership structures . These can include Youth Councils or other formal youth leadership groups that allow young people to contribute ideas, participate in planning, advise organizations, and take part in decision-making processes. According to YSA, grant recipients will use the funding to support the development of new Youth Councils or similar youth leadership structures, or the expansion of existing ones . This makes the opportunity relevant to organizations that already have some youth engagement experience but want to create a more formal mechanism for youth participation, as well as organizations that are ready to establish a new youth leadership structure. What Will Grant Recipients Be Expected to Do? Receiving the $2,000 grant comes with specific expectations. Organizations should therefore consider whether they have the capacity to develop a youth leadership structure and sustain youth engagement beyond a single event. 1. Create or Expand a Youth Leadership Structure Applicants will need to describe their plans for establishing or strengthening a formal youth advisory or leadership board, council, or similar group. The application asks organizations to explain: Their current programs and organizational work. Their existing experience with youth engagement. Their experience with youth voice and leadership. Their experience involving young people in decision-making. Whether they plan to create a new youth advisory structure or expand an existing one. What they hope the youth leadership structure will accomplish. How youth participation could strengthen the organization. The emphasis is therefore not simply on recruiting young people for an event. Applicants are expected to demonstrate how youth leadership can become part of their organization s continuing work. 2. Organize a Youth Leadership Summit Around MLK Day Each grantee will be expected to organize a citywide or statewide Youth Leadership Summit on or around MLK Day . YSA indicates that the Summit should be organized with the organization s youth leadership group. The program is therefore designed to give young people an active role in shaping the event rather than having adults independently plan the entire experience. The Summit can be scheduled between January 11 and January 25, 2027 , although YSA says it should take place as close as possible to MLK Day on January 18, 2027 . The Summit should provide training connected to: Youth-adult partnerships Youth voice Youth leadership Community service project design Future youth-led service opportunities The 200-Person Engagement Requirement One of the most important requirements applicants need to understand is the minimum engagement target. Grant recipients are expected to engage at least 200 youth and adults through the Youth Leadership Summit and/or related youth voice, leadership, and decision-making opportunities. The application specifically requires applicants to acknowledge this requirement and provide an estimate of how many youth and adults they expect to engage in relevant training or opportunities. The goal is not simply to establish a small internal youth council. The youth leadership group should also help broaden youth participation and encourage other young people and adults to become involved. YSA describes the program as requiring grantees to organize a Youth Leadership Summit and ongoing opportunities through The Civic Season while engaging a minimum of 200 youth and adults in commitments to future or ongoing service and related training. Continuing Youth Engagement Through The Civic Season The Youth At Every Decision-Making Table initiative extends beyond MLK Day. Applicants are asked to explain how their youth leadership group could continue engaging other young people after the Summit during the remainder of the 2026–2027 academic year and through The Civic Season, from Juneteenth through July 4 . This means applicants should think about a longer-term engagement strategy rather than proposing a single event. Potential activities described in an application could include continued youth leadership meetings, peer engagement, youth-led service projects, community conversations, leadership training, youth advisory activities, or other forms of participation that are consistent with the organization s mission. The key consideration is that the youth leadership group should help create opportunities for its peers as well. Who Can Apply for the Youth At Every Decision-Making Table Grant? The application identifies several types of organizations as eligible. These include: K-12 schools Higher education institutions Out-of-school-time programs Afterschool programs Summer learning programs Positive youth development organizations Community-based organizations Faith-based organizations State governments Local governments YSA s official program information confirms these organizational categories as eligible for the Youth At Every Decision-Making Table Grants. The application form also asks organizations to provide their organization name, organization type, contact information, mailing address, state, ZIP code, and website. Youth Representation and Inclusive Recruitment A major part of the application concerns how an organization will recruit young people who reflect the diversity of the community it serves. Applicants are asked to explain how they will recruit youth who are representative of their organization s or community s youth/student population. The application specifically identifies groups that applicants should consider reaching, including: Young people of color Young people from low-income families and neighborhoods Young people from rural areas Youth with disabilities Young people who are unhoused Young people in foster care Young people involved in the juvenile justice system Immigrants and refugees English Language Learners LGBTQ+ young people Young people from military families Other young people who are not typically asked to participate in leadership opportunities This component is important because the application is not simply asking organizations to create a youth council. Applicants must also explain how they will ensure that the council and related activities include young people whose perspectives may otherwise be overlooked. What Should Organizations Explain in Their Application? The application contains several substantive questions. Organizations should be prepared to address each area clearly and specifically. 1. Describe the Organization and Its Youth Engagement Experience Applicants must describe their organization, current programs, and previous experience with: Youth engagement Youth voice Youth leadership Youth decision-making This section provides an opportunity to demonstrate that the organization understands the needs of young people and has some capacity to work with them. 2. Explain the Youth Advisory or Leadership Structure Applicants must describe their plans and goals for creating or expanding a formal youth advisory board, leadership board, council, or similar group. The application asks organizations to explain: What they want to establish or expand. What they are excited about doing. What the youth group will contribute. How the planned actions will strengthen the organization. A strong response should therefore connect youth leadership directly to the organization s existing work rather than treating the youth group as a completely separate activity. 3. Explain How Youth Will Be Recruited Organizations must describe their recruitment strategy and explain how they will reach young people who represent the broader population they serve. This includes thinking about barriers that can prevent certain young people from participating and explaining how the organization will reach people who are traditionally underrepresented in leadership opportunities. 4. Describe the Youth Leadership Summit Applicants must provide preliminary ideas for a citywide or statewide Youth Leadership Summit taking place on or around MLK Day. The application emphasizes that the plans are preliminary because the event will ultimately be planned with the youth leadership group. Applicants should also explain how they intend to provide training to at least 200 youth and adults and encourage participants to commit to future or ongoing service. 5. Explain How Youth Will Engage Their Peers The application specifically asks organizations to consider what happens after the Summit. Applicants should provide ideas for how members of the youth leadership group can engage other young people throughout: The remainder of the 2026–2027 academic year The Civic Season from Juneteenth through July 4 This requirement reinforces the program s broader objective of expanding youth participation beyond a small leadership group. Grant Amount and Available Funding Each successful organization will receive a $2,000 grant . YSA states that $50,000 in total funding is available and that 25 citywide, regional, or statewide organizations will receive grants. The grant is funded through a federal AmeriCorps MLK Day of Service grant . Required $1,000 Match Funding Organizations applying for the grant must also be prepared to provide a $1,000 local match . The match can consist of: Cash contributions In-kind contributions Donated event supplies Food Recognition items for youth leadership group members or Summit participants Meeting space Event space Equipment Other qualifying local contributions Applicants must indicate whether they agree to meet the matching requirement and identify potential sources of the match. This means an organization applying for the $2,000 grant should consider how it will document an additional $1,000 in local support. What Can the $2,000 Grant Be Used For? The application asks applicants to submit a tentative $2,000 budget . A full budget will be submitted later if the organization is selected and enters into a grant agreement. However, the application clearly states that grant funds cannot be used for staff salaries and benefits . The funds also cannot be used for AmeriCorps-prohibited activities, including: Lobbying Partisan political activities Voter registration Applicants should therefore ensure that their proposed budget is directly connected to allowable activities supporting youth leadership, youth voice, decision-making, training, and related program implementation. Application Deadline The deadline for the Youth At Every Decision-Making Table Grant is: Sunday, October 25, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. local time. YSA s official MLK Day of Service page confirms the October 25 deadline and specifies that the deadline is based on the applicant s local time. Organizations should not wait until the final day if they need time to develop their youth leadership plans, identify match funding, prepare the preliminary budget, and collect organizational information. How to Apply Applications are submitted through the Youth Service America online application. The application requires organizations to provide organizational and contact information and answer questions about their current programs, youth engagement experience, proposed youth leadership structure, recruitment strategy, Youth Leadership Summit, continuing engagement plans, anticipated participant numbers, budget, and match funding. The application also provides options to: Save progress and return later. Resume a previously saved application. Applicants with questions about the application can contact Mike Minks at mminks@ysa.org . Apply through the Youth At Every Decision-Making Table Grant application Important Note About AI and the Application The application itself contains a specific request that applicants not use AI to prepare their application responses . YSA says it wants to hear about the applicant organization and its own ideas in the organization s own words. It also states that it does not use AI to review applications. Applicants should therefore treat the application questions as an opportunity to describe their actual organization, existing youth engagement work, local community, proposed plans, and ideas rather than submitting generic or AI-generated responses. For this reason, organizations should make sure that their final application responses genuinely reflect their own experience and plans. MLK Day of Service and the Wider Program Context The Youth At Every Decision-Making Table Grant is part of YSA s broader MLK Day of Service programming. The next MLK Day of Service will take place on January 18, 2027 . YSA describes MLK Day as a federal holiday designated as a National Day of Service and encourages Americans to participate in service and community action. YSA s broader work focuses on helping young people find their voices, take action, develop civic skills, and contribute to their communities. The organization says its campaigns and events have engaged more than 3.2 million young people in service over the past decade. The Youth At Every Decision-Making Table Grant fits within this broader approach by emphasizing not only youth service but also youth voice, leadership, participation, and decision-making . Why the Youth Council Component Matters One of the distinctive features of this opportunity is its emphasis on establishing a formal youth leadership structure. A one-time event can create an opportunity for young people to participate on a particular day. A youth council or similar structure can provide an ongoing mechanism through which young people can: Share perspectives with organizational leaders. Help identify community needs. Participate in planning. Develop leadership skills. Help design service projects. Engage their peers. Build relationships with adult partners. Continue participating in decision-making beyond MLK Day. The grant therefore combines organizational development, youth leadership development, community service, and ongoing civic participation . Suggested Areas Organizations Should Think About Before Applying Although the application requires organizations to provide their own responses, prospective applicants may find it useful to think through several practical questions before beginning. Organizational readiness Consider whether your organization already has: Youth programs Youth volunteers Youth advisory structures Adult staff or volunteers who work with young people Community partnerships Experience organizing service activities Youth leadership structure Consider: Whether a new Youth Council is needed Whether an existing youth group could be expanded How youth members would be selected How often the group would meet What decisions young people could influence How adult leaders would work with the youth group Recruitment Consider how the organization can reach young people who may not normally volunteer for leadership opportunities, particularly those identified in the application. Summit Consider: Where the Summit could take place Who should participate What training participants need How young people will help design the event How the organization can reach 200 or more participants How participants will be encouraged to continue serving afterward Long-term engagement Consider how the Youth Council could continue its work after MLK Day and through The Civic Season. Budget Consider how the $2,000 grant and $1,000 match could support allowable activities without being used for prohibited expenses. Key Dates and Requirements Item Details Grant Youth At Every Decision-Making Table Grant Grant amount $2,000 Total available funding $50,000 Expected grantees 25 organizations Required match $1,000 cash or in-kind MLK Day of Service January 18, 2027 Youth Leadership Summit period January 11–25, 2027, with the event encouraged to be as close to January 18 as possible Minimum engagement 200 youth and adults Continuing engagement Through the 2026–2027 academic year and The Civic Season Application deadline October 25, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. local time Staff salary/benefits Not eligible Lobbying Not eligible Partisan political activities Not eligible Voter registration Not eligible The dates and requirements above are based on YSA s current official program information and the application details provided for the 2026 grant cycle. Frequently Asked Questions How much funding does the grant provide? Each selected organization will receive $2,000 . How much funding is available overall? YSA states that $50,000 is available and that 25 organizations will receive grants. Is matching funding required? Yes. Applicants must provide and document $1,000 in local match funding , which may include cash or qualifying in-kind contributions. Who can apply? Eligible organizations listed by YSA include K-12 schools, higher education institutions, out-of-school-time/afterschool programs, positive youth development organizations, community-based organizations, faith-based organizations, state governments, and local governments. Learn more HERE Does the organization need an existing Youth Council? Not necessarily. The grant can support the development of new Youth Councils or similar youth leadership structures , as well as the expansion of existing ones. Is there a minimum number of people that must be engaged? Yes. The program requires engagement of at least 200 youth and adults through the Summit and/or related youth voice, leadership, and decision-making opportunities. When is MLK Day of Service? MLK Day of Service will be held on January 18, 2027 . When is the application deadline? The application deadline is Sunday, October 25, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. local time . Can grant money pay staff salaries? No. The application specifically states that grant funds cannot be used for staff salaries or benefits. Can the funding be used for lobbying or partisan political activities? No. The application identifies lobbying and partisan political activities among the prohibited uses of AmeriCorps funding. Conclusion The Youth At Every Decision-Making Table Grant 2026 provides an opportunity for eligible U.S. organizations to strengthen how young people participate in leadership, service, and decision-making. With $2,000 available to each selected organization , the program is designed to support the creation or expansion of Youth Councils and other formal youth leadership structures while connecting those structures to a broader Youth Leadership Summit around MLK Day and continuing engagement through The Civic Season. The opportunity goes beyond funding a single youth event. Applicants are expected to demonstrate how they will establish meaningful youth leadership, recruit participants who reflect the diversity of their communities, engage at least 200 youth and adults, provide relevant training, and continue creating opportunities for youth voice and leadership after the MLK Day period. Organizations considering applying should pay particular attention to the $1,000 match requirement , the 200-person engagement requirement , the restrictions on how grant funds can be spent, and the expectation that youth leadership structures will contribute to ongoing engagement throughout the 2026–2027 academic year and The Civic Season. The application deadline is October 25, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. local time , giving eligible organizations a clear opportunity to prepare their organizational information, youth leadership plans, recruitment strategy, Summit concept, preliminary budget, and match-funding plan before submission. title: University of Cambridge NERC-Funded PhD Studentships 2027: 15 Fully Funded CREATES Doctoral Opportunities in Environmental Science
summary: The University of Cambridge is offering 15 NERC-funded PhD studentships for students starting in October 2027 through the Cambridge Research Experience and Advanced Training for Environmental Scientists (CREATES) Doctoral Landscape Award (DLA) . Each studentship is designed to support 3.5 years of doctoral research in environmental science, with research opportunities hosted across relevant University of Cambridge departments and the British Antarctic Survey. The CREATES programme is the University of Cambridge s new environmental science doctoral training programme under the Natural Environment Research Council (NERC) Doctoral Landscape Awards . It succeeds the previous C-CLEAR programme and is designed to develop researchers working across major environmental challenges, including climate change, biodiversity, conservation, Earth sciences and environmental processes. For prospective PhD students interested in environmental research, climate science, conservation, geology, biodiversity, environmental modelling, plant sciences, zoology, archaeology and related areas, the 2027 CREATES DLA provides an opportunity to pursue doctoral study at Cambridge while being considered for NERC funding. University of Cambridge CREATES NERC PhD Studentships 2027 The Cambridge Research Experience and Advanced Training for Environmental Scientists (CREATES) is built around interdisciplinary environmental science research. The programme brings together the University of Cambridge and the British Antarctic Survey as hosts and works with a wider network of partners from areas including government, industry and the third sector. The programme addresses environmental challenges that have major implications for society, including: Climate change and environmental change Biodiversity loss Conservation Food production and land-use pressures Environmental and natural hazards Earth-system processes Polar and cryospheric science Environmental modelling and informatics Ecosystem processes Evolutionary and ecological research The CREATES programme is organised around three broad research themes: Solid Earth and Geological Hazards Climate Change and Environmental Processes Biology and Conservation These themes reflect the breadth of environmental research available through the programme. What Does the NERC-Funded PhD Opportunity Offer? For students beginning their studies in October 2027, Cambridge will offer: 15 NERC-funded PhD studentships 3.5 years of doctoral funding Research opportunities across eligible Cambridge departments and the British Antarctic Survey Access to the CREATES doctoral training environment Interdisciplinary environmental science training Opportunities to work with supervisors whose research aligns with NERC s remit Development of research, professional, technical and transferable skills The official programme states that the 2027 studentships will form part of a five-cohort CREATES programme replacing the previous C-CLEAR doctoral training programme. The wider CREATES programme also connects students with collaborative partners, providing opportunities for networking, professional development and, where applicable, internships and partner-led activities. Research Areas and Departments One of the major features of the CREATES DLA is the range of environmental research areas available to applicants. Current CREATES supervisors are associated with departments and research environments including: Department of Archaeology British Antarctic Survey Department of Chemistry Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics Department of Earth Sciences Department of Genetics Department of Geography Department of Plant Sciences Scott Polar Research Institute Department of Zoology This means prospective applicants can approach the programme from different academic backgrounds, provided their proposed research fits within the relevant environmental science and NERC remit. Examples of Potential Research Areas The current supervisor directory includes research areas such as: Climate and climate change Atmospheric science Ocean circulation Polar physical oceanography Palaeoenvironments Palaeobiology Conservation ecology Ecosystem-scale processes Environmental informatics Evolutionary biology Population genetics Behavioural ecology Marine ecology Plant and crop science Environmental physiology Geochemistry Volcanology Geological hazards Earth-surface processes Environmental microbiology Archaeology Quaternary science Cryosphere and climate research Applicants should examine the current supervisor and topic information carefully because the specific research interests and available supervision areas vary between academics. How the CREATES Research Topics Work An important feature of this PhD opportunity is that applicants are not necessarily applying to a completely finalised PhD project title . Instead, applicants are expected to identify topics and supervisors that particularly interest them. The final research project can then be developed with the supervisory team during the first term of doctoral study. This means applicants should focus on demonstrating: Their research interests Their understanding of the relevant environmental research area Why the topic interests them Which supervisors they would like to work with How their academic background relates to the proposed area Their potential to undertake independent doctoral research The programme strongly recommends contacting prospective supervisors before submitting an application. This allows applicants and supervisors to explore whether their research interests are compatible and can also provide useful advice about the application. What If a Prospective Supervisor Does Not Respond? The programme recognises that contacting academics can sometimes be difficult, particularly if a potential supervisor is conducting fieldwork or otherwise unavailable. Applicants who are interested in a particular area but cannot establish contact with a suitable supervisor can contact the CREATES DLA Administrator, who can help connect them with an academic. The administrator can be contacted at: dtp-admin@esc.cam.ac.uk NERC Research Remit Requirement Applicants seeking CREATES NERC DLA funding must ensure that at least one of their proposed research topics falls within the NERC research remit . Applicants may identify projects or research areas that fall under other UK Research Councils, but they will only be considered for CREATES DLA funding if at least one proposed subject area fits within NERC s remit. If admitted and funded through the DLA, the research topic must continue to remain within that remit during the development of the project. This makes it particularly important for applicants to understand the environmental science focus of NERC before selecting their preferred research topics. Cambridge PhD Admission Requirements Before applying for the NERC funding, applicants must first ensure that they meet the University s requirements for admission to the relevant PhD programme. According to the CREATES application guidance, applicants are expected to have: 1. A Strong Relevant Degree Applicants should normally have at least a 2.1 Honours degree from a UK university , or an equivalent qualification from an overseas university. The guidance gives CGPA 3.5/4.0 as an example of an equivalent overseas academic standard, although applicants should check the specific requirements applicable to their circumstances and chosen course. 2. Two Outstanding References Applicants need to provide two outstanding references . The programme recommends requesting references well in advance of the application deadline so that referees have enough time to prepare and submit them. 3. English-Language Proficiency Applicants must meet the University s English-language requirements. The exact evidence required can depend on the applicant s circumstances, previous education and course, so prospective international applicants should consult Cambridge s official English-language requirements before submitting their application. How to Apply for the Cambridge CREATES NERC PhD Applicants must apply through the University of Cambridge Applicant Portal and select the PhD course relevant to their preferred supervisor. The application process involves several important stages. Step 1: Research Supervisors and Topics Begin by examining the available CREATES topics and supervisors. Applicants are encouraged to: Identify research areas that match their interests. Review potential supervisors research interests. Identify more than one suitable topic where appropriate. Contact prospective supervisors. Discuss research interests and potential project directions. Develop a prioritised list of preferred supervisors and topics. The programme recommends providing a prioritised list because academic staff can act as lead supervisor for only one CREATES studentship per application round. Applicants may also identify supervisors in different departments. Step 2: Check the NERC Remit At least one proposed topic must fit within NERC s remit if the applicant wants to be considered for CREATES DLA funding. Step 3: Apply for the Relevant Cambridge PhD The application must be submitted through Cambridge s Applicant Portal. Applicants should select: Michaelmas Term 2027 start — 1 October 2027. Step 4: Request Funding Consideration When the application asks: “Do you wish to apply for funding?” applicants should select: “Yes — I wish to apply for funding.” Applicants should also indicate that they wish to be considered for the NERC Doctoral Landscape Award and identify their preferred CREATES topics and supervisors. Research Summary Required for the Application Applicants seeking DLA funding will need to provide information about their planned research interests. This includes: Prospective supervisor or supervisors Proposed topic or topics A 250-word summary of the area or areas of research they are interested in Some Cambridge departments may request a longer research proposal as part of their own admissions process, but the CREATES DLA specifically focuses on the applicant s 250-word research-interest summary. Applicants should therefore make sure that their 250-word summary is focused, relevant to NERC s remit and clearly connected to the research interests of their preferred supervisors. Where Should Applicants Enter Their Research Information? The exact structure of the Cambridge application form varies depending on the department and course. Applicants may encounter sections such as: Research Other Information Course-Specific Questions Additional Information to Support Your Application If a Research section is available, applicants should use it to provide information about their proposed supervisors, topics and research summary. If the Research section is not available, applicants should look for research-related questions under Course-Specific Questions . The Additional Information to Support Your Application section can also be used where applicants need more space to explain their preferred combinations of topics and supervisors. Applicants Should Complete the Entire Cambridge Application The CREATES guidance emphasises that the instructions concerning topics, supervisors and the 250-word summary do not replace the other questions in the University s PhD application. Applicants should answer all other questions required by their chosen Cambridge course. The funding section should also clearly indicate the applicant s interest in NERC funding and include preferred supervisors where requested. Funding and Financial Support The CREATES opportunity is a NERC-funded PhD studentship . The 2027 call provides 15 studentships, each lasting 3.5 years. The current Cambridge CREATES funding information explains that NERC studentships can cover tuition and provide a maintenance allowance and Research Training Support Grant. It also states that a limited number of studentships can be offered to international students, with UKRI funding covering the UK-rate fees, maintenance allowance and Research Training Support Grant; Cambridge has agreed to waive the difference between international and home fees for DLA students. Applicants should check the latest funding guidance for the precise conditions applying to the 2027 intake. International applicants should also note that certain expenses, such as visa and health-related surcharges, may not be covered by the DLA funding itself. Cambridge recommends that international applicants also consider other funding opportunities where appropriate. Important Application Deadlines The CREATES NERC DLA deadline is tied directly to the funding deadline for the applicant s chosen Cambridge course. For the 2027 entry cycle, the relevant deadline will be either 8 December 2026 or 6 January 2027 , depending on the course. Applicants must check the deadline for their first-choice course carefully. The final CREATES DLA deadline is therefore: 8 December 2026 or 6 January 2027, depending on the chosen Cambridge course. All supporting documentation, including references, must be submitted by the applicable deadline. Applicants should not assume that every Cambridge department uses the same deadline. Earlier Funding Deadlines Some other Cambridge funding schemes may have earlier deadlines. The CREATES guidance specifically highlights: The Department of Chemistry may have an earlier deadline for other PhD funding. The Department of Geography may have an earlier deadline for other PhD funding. US-based applicants seeking Gates Cambridge funding should apply by 14 October 2026, including references. Applicants interested in multiple funding sources should therefore research each relevant funding deadline rather than relying solely on the CREATES deadline. CREATES 2027 Application Timeline The programme has provided the following expected timeline for the 2027 intake: Supervisor Information Supervisor pages for the 2027 entry cycle were scheduled to be updated by: 1 September 2026 Application Deadline Depending on the selected course: 8 December 2026 or 6 January 2027 All supporting documents and references must be submitted by the relevant deadline. Interviews Online interviews are anticipated to take place during the week of: 22 February 2027 Offers Initial offers are expected to begin being communicated in late February 2027. The NERC Universal Acceptance Date is: Noon, 17 March 2027 What Does the CREATES Programme Look For in Applicants? Beyond minimum admission requirements, the CREATES DLA assessment process considers several aspects of a candidate s potential. The programme s assessment framework includes: Academic Excellence Applicants are assessed on factors such as: Degree results or predicted results Achievement in relevant subjects Academic achievements Research experience Evidence of advanced knowledge in the proposed research area Awareness of knowledge gaps and relevant methodologies Originality and Independence The programme looks for evidence of: Independent working ability Self-motivation Problem-solving Critical decision-making Independence during research or project work Communication Skills Applicants should be able to: Communicate clearly Explain complex ideas logically Provide precise and detailed answers Demonstrate enthusiasm for environmental science Preparedness for Doctoral Study The assessment also considers: Intellectual curiosity Ability to evaluate personal strengths and weaknesses Awareness of skills gaps Ability to identify challenges Ability to develop strategies for overcoming challenges Understanding of how doctoral study fits into future career plans Importantly, CREATES states that contextual information can also be taken into account. This can include adversity, caring responsibilities, employment undertaken alongside study, and differences in access to research opportunities. Why Contacting a Supervisor Before Applying Matters A strong supervisor match is an important part of the CREATES application process. Because applicants are expected to identify potential research areas and supervisors, contacting academics before applying can help applicants: Understand whether their research interests align. Learn more about potential projects. Discuss possible research directions. Determine whether a supervisor is accepting students. Decide which topics to prioritise. Develop a more focused research-interest statement. The programme itself strongly advises applicants to contact prospective supervisors before submitting an application. How to Prepare a Strong CREATES Application Applicants can begin preparing well before the deadline. 1. Research the Supervisors Read the profiles of potential supervisors carefully and identify academics whose research connects closely with your academic background and interests. 2. Identify Several Potential Topics Do not necessarily limit yourself to one research area. The programme encourages applicants to provide a prioritised list of topics and supervisors they would consider. 3. Check the NERC Remit Make sure at least one proposed research area clearly falls within NERC s remit. 4. Prepare Your 250-Word Research Summary The summary should communicate: What area you want to research Why the area interests you What environmental problem or research question motivates you How your interests relate to the supervisor Why the proposed area is appropriate for environmental science research 5. Request References Early Because two references are required, applicants should approach referees well before the relevant deadline. 6. Check the Exact Course Deadline The CREATES deadline is not necessarily identical across every Cambridge course. Applicants must identify the course associated with their first-choice supervisor and check whether the deadline is 8 December 2026 or 6 January 2027 . 7. Consider Other Cambridge Funding Applicants are encouraged to complete the Cambridge Trust and Gates Cambridge sections where relevant so they can be considered for additional sources of funding. However, some of these schemes have earlier deadlines. Learn more HERE An Opportunity for Environmental Science Researchers The CREATES DLA is designed around major environmental challenges and interdisciplinary scientific research. Its participating departments span areas from Earth sciences and climate research to biodiversity, conservation, genetics, plant sciences, zoology, archaeology and environmental modelling. The programme s broader training environment also aims to develop researchers who can work beyond academia. CREATES has collaborative relationships with organisations across government, industry, conservation and the third sector, creating opportunities for networking and professional development alongside doctoral research. Frequently Asked Questions When does the PhD start? The programme is for students beginning in October 2027 , with the application guidance specifying a 1 October 2027 Michaelmas Term start . How many studentships are available? There are 15 NERC-funded PhD studentships for the 2027 entry. How long is the funding? The studentships are for 3.5 years . Do I need to have a completely finished PhD project before applying? Not necessarily. Applicants identify topics and supervisors, while the final project is intended to be developed with the supervisory team during the first term. Can I apply to supervisors in different departments? Yes. The guidance allows applicants to choose supervisors across more than one department, although applicants should provide a prioritised list. Do I need a research topic within NERC s remit? Yes, if you want to be considered for CREATES NERC DLA funding, at least one proposed topic must fall within the NERC remit. Is an English-language requirement applicable? Yes. Applicants must meet Cambridge s English-language requirements where applicable. When is the application deadline? The applicable CREATES deadline is the same as the funding deadline for the applicant s chosen course: 8 December 2026 or 6 January 2027 . When are interviews expected? Online interviews are anticipated during the week of 22 February 2027 . When will offers be made? Initial offers are expected from late February, with the NERC Universal Acceptance Date at noon on 17 March 2027 . Because the final application deadline depends on the chosen Cambridge course, prospective applicants should check carefully whether their deadline is 8 December 2026 or 6 January 2027 .
