Establish Your Geoeconomics Focus Your research should clearly connect to geoeconomics. Applicants can consider how their work relates to issues such as economic security, trade, sanctions, industrial policy, global finance, energy, climate transition or defence economics. 2. Prepare a Strong Research Project Sketch The one-page project sketch should clearly communicate the research or policy project you intend to develop. The limited length means that applicants should present the central idea clearly and avoid unnecessary detail. 3. Demonstrate Research Quality The CV and writing sample should provide evidence of your academic and research track record. A writing sample such as a third-year paper or job market paper can demonstrate your ability to formulate and investigate a research question. 4. Select Appropriate References Choose two potential references who can credibly speak to your academic or research capabilities. 5. Explain Your Motivation The cover letter should establish why specialised training in geoeconomics would be relevant to your research development. 6. Confirm Your Institutional Eligibility Applicants should verify that they will be enrolled or employed at an eligible European institution and that they can participate alongside their existing PhD or Postdoctoral position. 7. Plan for the In-Person Components Because on-site attendance is expected, applicants should be prepared to participate in the in-person modules throughout the programme year. The programme provides travel and accommodation support for these modules. Read Full Details About This Opportunity And Apply HERE Conclusion The Next-Geo Program 2027 is a specialised one-year research and training fellowship designed for advanced PhD students and early Postdoctoral researchers working on geoeconomics in Europe. Coordinated by the Kiel Institute in cooperation with CEPR, Bocconi University and the Oxford University Department of Economics, and funded by Stiftung Mercator, the programme aims to strengthen the next generation of researchers working at the intersection of economics and geopolitics. Participants receive access to advanced lectures, research training, senior mentoring, networking opportunities and policy engagement. Promising projects may also receive research assistant support and funding for data purchases and/or AI subscriptions. Travel and accommodation for the programme s in-person modules are covered, while participants can remain enrolled or employed at their home institutions. The programme follows a structured annual cycle beginning with a winter online kick-off, continuing through spring research training and summer policy workshops, and concluding with the Kiel-CEPR Conference on Geoeconomics in autumn. Participants develop a research or policy project throughout the programme, with selected projects potentially presented at conferences or developed into working papers or policy briefs. The application deadline is October 31, 2026 , with applications submitted by that date guaranteed full consideration. The organisers aim to finalise the 2027 cohort by the end of November 2026. For researchers who meet the academic and institutional requirements, the programme provides a structured opportunity to deepen their expertise in geoeconomics while developing a research or policy project and connecting with a wider European network of scholars, policymakers and practitioners. title: Elliot L. Richardson Leadership Lab 2026: Fully Funded Public Service Leadership Opportunity for Undergraduate and Graduate Students in Washington, D.C.
summary: The Elliot L. Richardson Leadership Lab 2026 is inviting nominations for a select group of undergraduate and graduate students interested in public service, government, public administration, civic engagement and community impact. Hosted by the National Academy of Public Administration (NAPA) , the Leadership Lab will take place on November 8, 2026, in Washington, D.C. The programme is designed to expose emerging public service leaders to accomplished scholars, practitioners and public servants while providing practical leadership development, mentorship, networking and opportunities to engage with the wider public administration community. Participation is by nomination only . Students cannot simply submit an ordinary individual application; their college or university must nominate them for consideration. The nomination deadline is September 25, 2026 . The Leadership Lab is particularly relevant for students who see themselves pursuing careers in government, public administration, public policy or other areas of public service and who want to develop the knowledge, relationships and leadership skills needed to contribute to complex public-sector challenges. About the Elliot L. Richardson Leadership Lab The Elliot L. Richardson Leadership Lab is an initiative of the National Academy of Public Administration , an organisation focused on strengthening public administration and public service. The programme is named after Elliot L. Richardson , whose public service career included service in four Cabinet-level positions in the United States government. The National Academy s separate Elliot L. Richardson Prize recognises public service virtues associated with his legacy, including excellence, integrity and dedication to the public good. The Leadership Lab takes this legacy into a student-focused setting by bringing emerging public service leaders together with experienced figures in government, public administration and related fields. According to NAPA, the Lab is intended for the next generation of leaders who want to shape government , rather than simply work within government. What Is the Richardson Leadership Lab? The Richardson Leadership Lab is an exclusive, invitation-only leadership experience for a select group of undergraduate and graduate students nominated by their colleges and universities. The programme combines: Leadership development Interactive exercises Real-world scenarios Conversations with experienced public servants Mentorship Professional networking Public administration perspectives Exposure to the wider public service community Rather than being structured as a conventional classroom course, the Lab emphasises direct interaction with accomplished scholars and practitioners. Students have the opportunity to hear from people with substantial experience in public service and to explore how leadership operates when public officials and organisations face complex challenges. Date and Location The 2026 Richardson Leadership Lab is scheduled for: Date: November 8, 2026 Time: 9:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. Location: National Academy of Sciences Address: 2101 Constitution Ave. NW, Washington, DC 20418 The Lab is also incorporated into NAPA s 2026 National Conference, which runs from November 8–10, 2026 . Selected students are invited to remain for the full National Conference at no cost. Who Is the Leadership Lab Designed For? The programme is designed for undergraduate and graduate students who demonstrate leadership potential and a serious interest in public service. NAPA specifically describes the target audience as students studying public administration and other related fields . The nomination criteria also emphasise students who demonstrate interest in: Public service Government Civic engagement Community impact Leadership Creating meaningful change This means the programme is not simply looking for students based on their academic programme. The nomination process also considers the student s demonstrated interest in public service and potential to contribute to the field. What Will Participants Experience? Selected students will participate in a series of activities designed to strengthen their understanding of public service leadership. 1. Learn From Accomplished Public Service Leaders Participants will have opportunities to learn directly from experienced leaders who have worked across: Government Public administration Academia Public service The programme provides students with perspectives that may not normally be available through university coursework alone. The emphasis is on practical leadership lessons and real-world experiences rather than purely theoretical discussions. 2. Develop Practical Leadership Skills The Lab uses interactive exercises and real-world scenarios to help students explore the challenges involved in public service leadership. Participants can examine how leaders: Respond to difficult situations Navigate complexity Deal with change Manage competing demands Approach ethical questions Build public trust Work toward meaningful outcomes NAPA describes the programme as an opportunity to build practical leadership skills that participants can apply beyond the event. 3. Engage With Senior Scholars and Practitioners A major component of the Leadership Lab is direct engagement with experienced figures in public administration and public service. Students can participate in discussions with scholars and practitioners and gain exposure to professional perspectives on leadership, government and public administration. The programme s format includes several opportunities for direct interaction rather than simply listening to formal presentations. 4. Participate in Interactive Roundtables The programme includes interactive roundtables that connect students and early-career professionals with experienced public servants. These small-group discussions are designed to facilitate meaningful dialogue and mentorship. The roundtable format can give students opportunities to ask questions, discuss challenges and learn from the experiences of people who have worked in public service. 5. Explore Ethical and High-Impact Leadership The programme places particular emphasis on leadership with integrity and impact . Participants are expected to explore what it means to lead when public-sector decisions involve difficult choices, changing circumstances and competing priorities. The Lab s discussions address themes such as: Ethical leadership Public trust Leadership during challenging circumstances Navigating change Institutional responsibility Public impact These themes are consistent with NAPA s description of the programme as preparing students to become leaders capable of addressing consequential public-service challenges. Signature Leadership Conversation One of the programme highlights is a Signature Leadership Conversation . This is described as a fireside-style discussion featuring nationally recognised public leaders. The conversation focuses on practical experiences involving: Ethical leadership Public trust Navigating contemporary challenges Lessons from public service careers The format is intended to give students an opportunity to hear directly from experienced leaders rather than relying exclusively on textbook perspectives. Leadership Snapshots The Leadership Lab also includes Leadership Snapshots , which provide fast-paced reflections from senior and rising leaders. Topics identified by NAPA include: Crisis leadership Rebuilding trust in institutions Innovation Learning through failure These sessions allow participants to encounter different perspectives on leadership and the experiences that shape effective public service professionals. Interactive Roundtables and Mentorship Another important part of the programme is its interactive roundtable component. Students can connect directly with experienced public servants and participate in conversations designed around: Leadership Public service Professional development Real-world challenges Mentorship The programme therefore provides both formal learning and relationship-building opportunities. What Participants Can Gain According to NAPA, students who participate in the Richardson Leadership Lab can leave the experience with several forms of professional and educational development. These include: Stronger Leadership Foundation Participants can develop a stronger foundation in practical leadership and acquire tools that can be applied to future academic, professional and public-service activities. Greater Understanding of Public Service The programme provides exposure to the public service profession and to challenges facing future government leaders. Connections With Experienced Leaders Participants can develop connections with public administration scholars, practitioners and public service leaders. Peer Network Students join a select cohort of other emerging leaders with an interest in public service and public impact. Broader Professional Network The programme can introduce students to a wider network that may continue developing throughout their careers. Exposure to NAPA s Community Participants become exposed to the broader National Academy of Public Administration community and conversations concerning public administration and the future of government. Opportunity to Attend the NAPA National Conference An important component of the programme is the opportunity for selected Leadership Lab participants to attend NAPA s National Conference . The National Academy states that selected students are invited to stay for the full conference from November 8–10, 2026, at no cost . The conference brings together individuals from: Government Academia Business Nonprofit organisations The event examines major issues affecting public administration and the future of government. The National Conference schedule confirms that the Richardson Leadership Lab takes place on November 8, followed by other conference activities through November 10. Travel and Accommodation Support The Leadership Lab provides significant logistical support for selected participants. NAPA states that travel and accommodations will be covered by the Academy . This is an important feature for students who would otherwise face the cost of travelling to Washington, D.C., and arranging accommodation for the event. The programme information provided by NAPA does not state that every possible personal expense is covered. Therefore, applicants should review the official programme information and any instructions provided after nomination regarding the exact travel and accommodation arrangements. The Nomination Process The Richardson Leadership Lab is not an open self-application programme . Participation is by nomination. Students must be nominated by their college or university for consideration. This means that students interested in participating should contact the appropriate person or office at their institution early enough for their institution to complete the nomination. The official nomination form collects information from the nominator as well as information about the student. Who Can Nominate a Student? The nomination form asks the nominator to provide: Full name Title or role Institution or university Department or programme Email address Phone number Relationship to the nominee Length of time they have known the student This information allows NAPA to understand the relationship between the nominator and the student being recommended. Information Required About the Student The nomination form requests information including: Student s full name Preferred name Email address Phone number University Degree programme Expected graduation year Students should therefore make sure their university and academic information is accurate and up to date before the nomination is submitted. The questions include: Why is the student being nominated? The nominator must provide 250–500 words explaining why the student is being nominated for the Richardson Leadership Lab. How has the student demonstrated interest in public service, civic engagement or community impact? The nominator must provide approximately 250 words describing the student s involvement or interest in these areas. What distinguishes the student from peers? However, applicants should distinguish this from a conventional scholarship or fellowship that provides a cash stipend. title: Upfront Ventures Founder Fellows 2026: $75,000+ Startup Backing for the Next Generation of Technical Builders and Researchers
summary: The Upfront Ventures Founder Fellows programme is inviting applications for its second cohort , offering an eight-week fellowship designed for the next generation of technical builders, engineers, researchers and aspiring startup founders. The programme is aimed at highly capable individuals who are already building, researching or working in high-growth technology environments and are considering starting a venture-backed company. Over the course of eight weeks, selected Fellows will receive exposure to Upfront Ventures partners , participate in the Upfront Summit , take part in intimate conversations with category-defining founders and gain access to a network of builders and operators. A major feature of the programme is the opportunity for Fellows to receive $75,000 or more in backing when they incorporate a venture-backable startup . This makes the fellowship particularly relevant to technically strong individuals who may already have significant experience but are at different stages of deciding when and how to launch a company. What Is the Upfront Ventures Founder Fellows Programme? The Upfront Ventures Founder Fellows is an eight-week programme created by Upfront Ventures for individuals who represent the next generation of technical founders and researchers. The fellowship is designed around exposure, relationships and preparation for entrepreneurship. Rather than requiring every participant to already have an incorporated company, the programme appears to target people who are at different stages of their transition toward becoming founders. The profiles highlighted by Upfront include: Recent graduates with experience at hyper-growth startups. Individuals who have left school to work full-time at leading AI laboratories. Highly accomplished technical builders. Engineers working at rapidly growing technology companies. Individuals who want to start a company but are not yet ready to take the leap. Technical researchers and builders with the potential to create venture-backable startups. The second cohort therefore brings together people who may have different educational and professional paths but share an interest in building significant technology companies. What Does the Founder Fellows Programme Offer? The fellowship lasts for eight weeks . During this period, Fellows receive opportunities to interact with Upfront s investment network and the broader technology and startup ecosystem. The programme includes several key components. 1. Direct Exposure to Upfront Partners Fellows receive direct exposure to Upfront s partners . This gives participants an opportunity to engage with people at the venture capital firm and gain exposure to perspectives surrounding technology, entrepreneurship and company building. For aspiring founders, access to experienced investors can provide an opportunity to better understand how venture-backed companies are developed and supported. 2. Attendance at the Upfront Summit Fellows will also attend the Upfront Summit . The summit is an important part of Upfront s wider network and provides Fellows with an opportunity to interact with people across the startup and investment ecosystem. For participants considering founding a company, attending a major gathering connected to investors, founders and technology leaders can provide opportunities for conversations and relationship building. 3. Fireside Chats With Category-Defining Founders Another feature of the programme is access to intimate fireside chats with category-defining founders . These sessions are intended to expose Fellows to the experiences and perspectives of founders who have built companies that have established significant positions within their respective categories. For technical builders who are considering entrepreneurship, these conversations can provide insight into the realities of starting and developing a company. 4. Access to a Network of Builders and Operators Fellows will also be able to plug into Upfront s network of builders and operators . This is an important component of the fellowship because startup creation is not limited to technical development. Building a company can involve product development, hiring, operations, fundraising, go-to-market strategy, partnerships and many other areas. Access to a network of people who have experience building and operating companies can therefore expose Fellows to perspectives beyond their own technical discipline. $75,000+ Startup Backing One of the most significant elements highlighted in the programme announcement is Upfront s commitment to back Fellows with $75,000 or more when they incorporate a venture-backable startup . The announcement states: we ll back you with $75,000+ when you incorporate a venture-backable startup! This means the fellowship is connected directly to potential financial backing for Fellows who go on to incorporate a startup that meets the relevant venture-backability criteria. It is important to distinguish this from a general cash award or unrestricted fellowship stipend. The information provided describes the $75,000+ support specifically in connection with incorporating a venture-backable startup . Applicants should review the official fellowship terms and application information for the precise conditions associated with this backing. Who Is Upfront Looking For? The programme announcement identifies several types of candidates. Rather than describing a single conventional applicant profile, Upfront highlights three examples of the kinds of people it wants to attract. The Founder The first profile is the aspiring founder who is already demonstrating strong professional experience. According to Upfront, this person may be: Graduating from university. Equipped with multiple internships at hyper-growth startups. Preparing to start a company as soon as possible. Already oriented toward entrepreneurship. Interested in building a venture-backable startup. This profile is particularly relevant to technically talented graduates who have used internships to gain experience inside rapidly growing startups and are now considering founding their own company. The Dropout The second profile is the technical individual who has left formal education to pursue work at a leading AI laboratory. Upfront describes this candidate as someone who: Left school. Joined a leading AI lab full-time. Is among the strongest builders in their environment. Has recognition from other people within the technical community. Has the potential to become a startup founder. This profile demonstrates that a traditional university graduation pathway is not necessarily the only route into the fellowship. The emphasis is instead on demonstrated technical ability, ambition and potential to build. The Engineer The third example is an engineer who has already entered the technology industry. This person may have: Recently graduated. Joined a hyper-growth startup. Developed professional experience as an engineer. Considered starting a company. Not yet reached the point where they are ready to leave their current role and launch a startup. This profile is particularly relevant to people who are interested in entrepreneurship but want to spend more time developing their experience before making the transition into founding. What Kind of People Should Consider Applying? Based on the profiles provided by Upfront, the programme is particularly oriented toward people with strong technical capabilities and an interest in company building. Potential applicants may include: Technical founders preparing to launch a startup. Software engineers working at high-growth technology companies. AI builders and researchers working on advanced technologies. Recent graduates with strong startup experience. Startup engineers considering entrepreneurship. Former students or dropouts who have moved into high-level technical roles. Researchers and technical builders who have the potential to develop venture-backable companies. Aspiring founders who are not yet ready to incorporate but are seriously considering doing so. The examples in the announcement suggest that Upfront is looking for demonstrated ability rather than simply academic credentials. Why the Technical Builder Profile Matters The programme s description places considerable emphasis on technical ability . Rather than focusing primarily on conventional business experience, the profiles highlight: Engineering experience. AI laboratory experience. Startup internships. Technical building ability. Experience at hyper-growth technology companies. The potential to create venture-backable startups. This makes the programme particularly relevant to individuals who have built technical expertise and are considering turning that expertise into a company. Eight Weeks of Founder Development and Exposure The programme runs for eight weeks , providing a defined period during which Fellows can engage with Upfront s ecosystem. The fellowship combines several types of exposure: Investment ecosystem exposure Fellows interact directly with Upfront partners. Founder exposure Participants join intimate conversations with established founders. Community exposure Fellows connect with builders and operators. Conference exposure Participants attend the Upfront Summit. Entrepreneurial opportunity Fellows can potentially receive $75,000+ in backing when they incorporate a venture-backable startup. This combination creates a programme centred on the transition from technical talent toward venture-backed entrepreneurship. The Upfront Summit The Upfront Summit is included as part of the fellowship experience. For Fellows, participation in the summit provides an opportunity to engage with a broader community connected to Upfront and the startup ecosystem. It also complements the programme s other activities, particularly the founder conversations and networking opportunities. Networking With Builders and Operators A central feature of the fellowship is access to Upfront s network. The programme specifically mentions connecting Fellows with: Builders. Operators. Founders. Upfront partners. For someone considering starting a company, these relationships can be relevant across multiple stages of company creation. A technical founder may, for example, need to develop relationships with other engineers, product specialists, operators, investors and experienced founders as their company develops. What Makes the Programme Different From a Traditional Fellowship? The Founder Fellows programme is closely connected to venture creation. It is not presented simply as an educational programme or professional development course. Its structure combines: Technical talent identification. Founder networking. Investor exposure. Founder conversations. Startup ecosystem access. Participation in the Upfront Summit. Potential financial backing for a venture-backable startup. The $75,000+ commitment is particularly significant because it connects participation in the fellowship with a potential pathway toward startup financing. Application Deadline No application deadline is stated . The announcement says that applications are open and directs prospective Fellows to apply, but it does not provide a closing date. Applicants should therefore check the official application page for the latest deadline or any indication that applications may close once the cohort is filled. Qualifications and Experience Although no formal academic qualification is specified in the announcement, the candidate profiles indicate a strong emphasis on technical achievement and relevant experience. Potentially relevant backgrounds include: Engineering. Artificial intelligence. Technical research. Software development. Startup experience. Hyper-growth technology companies. AI laboratories. Technical product development. Entrepreneurship. The examples suggest that applicants should be able to demonstrate significant technical ability, rather than relying solely on academic credentials. Who Is the Programme Designed For? In broad terms, the Founder Fellows programme is designed for the next generation of technical founders, builders and researchers . It may be particularly relevant to someone who fits one or more of the following descriptions: A technically strong graduate with startup experience. An engineer at a high-growth technology company. An AI researcher or builder. A former student now working at a leading AI laboratory. A technically accomplished individual preparing to launch a startup. An aspiring founder who has not yet incorporated a company. A builder who wants access to experienced founders, operators and venture investors. Important Things Applicants Should Know Before applying, prospective Fellows should understand several important points. 1. The programme lasts eight weeks Applicants should be prepared to engage with the fellowship throughout its programme period. 2. It is focused on technical talent The programme specifically targets technical builders and researchers. 3. Startup ambitions are central The candidate descriptions are oriented toward people who either want to start companies or have the potential to do so. 4. The programme includes investor exposure Fellows receive direct exposure to Upfront partners. 5. The programme includes founder access Participants take part in intimate fireside conversations with category-defining founders. 6. Financial backing is connected to startup formation Upfront states that it will back Fellows with $75,000+ when they incorporate a venture-backable startup . 7. No deadline is stated in the supplied announcement Applicants should check the application page for the current closing arrangements. Application portal HERE Prospective applicants should use the official form to submit their application and review any requirements or additional information provided by Upfront during the application process. Conclusion The Upfront Ventures Founder Fellows programme is an eight-week fellowship aimed at identifying and supporting the next generation of technical builders, engineers, researchers and aspiring founders. The programme combines direct exposure to Upfront partners , attendance at the Upfront Summit , intimate conversations with experienced founders and access to a network of builders and operators. Its target audience includes technically accomplished graduates, engineers at hyper-growth startups, AI researchers and builders, and individuals who have taken unconventional educational or professional routes into advanced technical work. A distinctive part of the opportunity is Upfront s stated commitment to provide $75,000+ in backing when a Fellow incorporates a venture-backable startup , connecting the fellowship with a potential pathway toward venture creation. Applications for the second cohort are open , although the announcement provided does not specify an application deadline. Interested technical builders and researchers should review the official application form promptly for current requirements and closing information. title: Prince Casper Foundation Impact Grant 2026/2027: ₦6 Million Education Grant for Educators Supporting Underserved Rural Communities in Nigeria
summary: The Prince Casper Foundation Impact Grant 2026/2027 is an educator-led funding opportunity designed to support teachers and other education-sector professionals working to improve learning outcomes for children and young people in underserved and educationally disadvantaged communities across Nigeria. The grant provides a total of ₦6 million to successful applicants across three funding tiers. Funding is intended to help educators address practical challenges affecting teaching and learning, including access to learning resources, digital technology, school infrastructure, teacher development, student-focused initiatives, inclusion, and other locally relevant educational needs. Applications for the 2026/2027 cycle opened on 21 September 2026 and close on 6 November 2026 . About the Prince Casper Foundation Impact Grant The Impact Grant is established by the Prince Casper Foundation , a nonprofit organization focused on advancing equitable and quality education, particularly for children and young people in underserved communities. Rather than providing general-purpose funding, the Impact Grant is designed to place resources directly in the hands of educators who understand the educational challenges facing their students and communities. The Foundation describes the grant as an opportunity to fund work that is already taking shape in classrooms and communities and help educators carry those initiatives further. The overarching purpose is to improve educational outcomes for students in rural, underserved, or otherwise educationally disadvantaged communities in Nigeria. What the Impact Grant Supports The 2026/2027 Impact Grant is organized around four priority focus areas . Applicants proposed projects should demonstrate relevance to one or more of these areas. 1. Learning Access The Learning Access focus area addresses barriers that prevent students from participating effectively in education. Projects may seek to improve: Classroom readiness Access to essential learning materials Literacy development Student attendance Learning environments Resources that help students participate more effectively in school The objective is to address practical barriers that can interfere with students ability to learn and remain engaged in education. 2. Digital Innovation Digital Innovation focuses on using technology to address educational challenges and prepare students for an increasingly technology-driven economy. Potential initiatives may include: Digital learning resources ICT infrastructure Digital literacy Technology-enabled teaching E-learning initiatives Innovative approaches to classroom learning Projects designed to reduce the digital divide The Foundation s broader education programmes also identify digital literacy training, ICT infrastructure, e-learning, blended learning, and mobile learning as areas of interest. 3. Educator Excellence The Educator Excellence category focuses on improving teaching quality, classroom engagement, and educational leadership. Projects can address areas such as: Teacher professional development Instructional improvement Classroom engagement Teaching resources School leadership Professional learning Practical approaches that strengthen educational delivery This reflects the Foundation s wider emphasis on teacher development, continuous professional development, teaching grants, and recognition of educators. 4. Inclusive Empowerment Inclusive Empowerment focuses on educational equity and initiatives that help students and families overcome barriers to participation and long-term development. This may include projects that: Reduce student dropout Promote educational inclusion Support vulnerable learners Address barriers affecting disadvantaged students Improve opportunities for girls and other underserved groups Build longer-term resilience within families and communities The Foundation s broader mission also includes supporting girls, children with disabilities, inclusive education, and initiatives that address socioeconomic and geographic barriers to education. How Much Funding Is Available? A total of ₦6 million is available for the 2026/2027 Impact Grant cycle. The funding will be distributed among 26 successful applicants across three grant tiers . Applicants do not choose which tier they want to receive. Instead, the selection committee determines the appropriate funding level based on factors such as the proposed project s: Scope Cost Educational need Relevance Potential impact Grant Tier 1: Trailblazer Grant amount: ₦500,000 per successful applicant Number of grantees: 7 Total allocation: ₦3,500,000 The Trailblazer tier is intended for larger or more transformational projects capable of producing sustainable educational change and potentially inspiring similar initiatives elsewhere. Grant Tier 2: Catalyst Grant amount: ₦200,000 per successful applicant Number of grantees: 6 Total allocation: ₦1,200,000 The Catalyst tier is designed to support promising initiatives with potential for development, growth, and longer-term impact. Grant Tier 3: Launchpad Grant amount: ₦100,000 per successful applicant Number of grantees: 13 Total allocation: ₦1,300,000 The Launchpad tier provides smaller-scale seed funding intended to help educators turn early-stage concepts and classroom needs into practical initiatives. Who Can Apply? The Impact Grant is primarily designed for educators and education-sector professionals in Nigeria who are directly contributing to the learning, development, or educational outcomes of children and young people in primary or secondary education . According to the Foundation s current eligibility criteria, applicants must: Be actively involved in the education sector in Nigeria. Applicants should be directly involved in or contributing to the education, learning, development, or educational outcomes of children and young people in primary or secondary education. Work in an underserved or disadvantaged community. The applicant must be serving or working within a rural, underserved, or otherwise educationally disadvantaged community in Nigeria. Demonstrate genuine financial need. Applicants must show that financial constraints are affecting their ability to support or improve teaching and learning outcomes. Present a relevant educational initiative or need. The proposed project should address a genuine educational challenge and align with the Foundation s mission and one or more of its four focus areas. Demonstrate capacity to deliver the proposed project. The selection process considers the applicant s track record and evidence that they can realistically implement the proposed initiative. Prince Casper Fellows are also eligible to apply, although the Foundation states that priority will be given to applicants who have not previously received the Impact Grant. What Kind of Applicants Is the Grant Looking For? The opportunity is particularly relevant to educators who are already working directly with students and have identified a specific problem that additional funding could help address. Examples could include educators seeking resources for: Classroom learning materials Science or other subject-specific equipment Digital learning initiatives Technology and ICT resources Literacy programmes Student support initiatives Teacher training or professional development Infrastructure improvements Projects addressing barriers to school participation Initiatives supporting vulnerable or underserved learners Practical projects designed to improve educational outcomes The Foundation s previous grant projects illustrate the range of interventions that can be supported. Previous initiatives have included practical science laboratory equipment, classroom resources, learning recovery programmes, student transportation solutions, and other education-focused interventions. How Applications Are Evaluated The Impact Grant uses a merit-based evaluation framework. The Foundation identifies several criteria that are considered when reviewing applications. 1. Demonstration of Need — 20% Applicants should clearly establish the educational challenge they are addressing and explain the severity and urgency of the problem. A strong application therefore needs to make the problem understandable rather than simply stating that additional funding is required. 2. Relevance and Alignment — 10% The proposed initiative should align with the Impact Grant s focus areas and the broader mission of the Prince Casper Foundation. 3. Impact Potential and Sustainability — 30% This is the largest component of the published evaluation framework. Applicants should demonstrate how the project can create meaningful educational change and whether its benefits can continue beyond the period of grant funding. 4. Feasibility and Implementation Plan — 20% The Foundation considers whether the proposed project can realistically be delivered. Applicants should therefore provide a credible plan, appropriate activities, and a realistic timeline that matches the identified educational need. 5. Applicant Capacity and Track Record — 10% The Foundation considers evidence that the applicant has the ability and experience necessary to implement the proposed initiative. This component may be assessed during the interview and reference-check stages. 6. Budget Clarity and Accountability — 10% The proposed budget should be properly costed and proportionate to the project. Applicants should also demonstrate that they can account responsibly for grant funds. Application Requirements The application process is conducted online through the Foundation s application portal. Applicants are expected to provide supporting information and documentation as part of their submission. The Foundation currently identifies the following key materials: Letter of Intent Applicants are required to submit a 500–750 word Letter of Intent explaining: The educational challenge they are addressing Their proposed solution The expected impact of the project The letter should provide a clear connection between the identified problem, the proposed intervention, and the expected educational outcomes. Curriculum Vitae Applicants must provide a CV containing relevant information such as: Professional background Teaching experience Relevant achievements Educational or community involvement The application instructions also request a recent headshot. Supporting Materials Applicants may upload additional materials demonstrating their qualifications, experience, previous work, or potential impact. The Foundation requests that supporting materials be submitted as a single PDF where applicable. APPLY HERE Application Timeline and Deadline The current 2026/2027 application period is: Opening date: 21 September 2026 Closing date: 6 November 2026 Deadline: 6 November 2026 The Foundation has listed the announcement of winners as TBA , meaning a specific winner-announcement date has not yet been provided on the current grant page. Applicants should therefore prepare their materials in advance rather than waiting until the final day of the application period. Read Full Details About This Opportunity HERE Why This Grant Matters for Rural Education Many education challenges are highly localized. A teacher working directly with students may understand a classroom s needs more clearly than an outside organization because they experience those challenges every day. The Impact Grant is structured around this principle by directing funding toward educators who are already working within the communities they seek to support. Previous recipients provide examples of how this model can translate funding into practical educational interventions. The Foundation s published 2025 Impact Grant results show projects involving science laboratory equipment, classroom learning materials, student support, and other community-specific initiatives. title: 2027 Summer Philanthropy Internship at Constellation: Paid 10-Week Opportunity for Students in the United States
